newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends weaker, but run-up intact.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends weaker, but run-up intact.

text.p: COMEX copper closed weaker Friday despite hitting fresh one-year highs in the July contract, which ended a touch higher for the week despite overbought signals dogging the charts.

COMEX July copper settled 0.15 cent lower at 119.10 cents per pound, traded 120.40 to 118.00 cents. Spot June went out 0.30 cent weaker at 118.60 cents. Volume was moderate at an estimated 10,000 lots.
August and all contracts further forward ended higher.
July's 9-day RSI ended the week at 75.44 percent, still well within overbought territory.

COMEX June switched into contango over July this week despite an LME steadfastly in backwardation. The move was fuelled by Cerro Sales Corp liquidation nearby long positions ahead of the company's official merger with MG June 1, floor sources said.
Cerro's liquidation, which has been influencing nearby COMEX, was set to end this week, dealers said.

Mo Ahmadzadeh of Rudolf Wolff said producer selling and producer insurance programs have capped the market in the first half of next year, while nearby, the market was focused on the open interest at $2,600 in LME June call options.
"My expectation is that after Wednesday the forwards will be lent and the price could easily dip down two cents (per lb)," Ahmadzadeh said.
The U.S. physical market remains tight for the time being with cathode premiums over spot COMEX at 2.75 to 3.50 cents.
On June 3 Canadian Noranda Inc's Horne smelter will close for a 15-day planned maintenance. "There will be no loss of production at the refinery," a smelter spokesman said.
LME stocks continued to fall this week, albeit in a more modest, haphazard way. Stocks Friday rose 200 tonnes to 133,225 tonnes.
